- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.10 → -0.20 → +0.10), model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment’s recent average, not peak.
